topics.concept: A bar chart maps values to bar lengths, and in a terminal those bars are built from repeated block characters scaled to the data range. Choosing the scale, handling negatives, and labeling axes well are what separate a readable chart from a wall of blocks. It is the fastest way to compare a handful of categories without any graphics library.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded category values with labels, renders horizontal and vertical ASCII bars with automatic scaling, and handles negative and zero values gracefully.
topics.name: ASCII Bar Chart Builder
topics.real_world_use: Engineers embed ASCII bars in CLI reports and log summaries where graphics are unavailable.

topics.concept: A sparkline compresses a whole time series into a few characters using block elements of increasing height. A row of sparklines in a table lets a reader scan trends across dozens of metrics at once. They trade precision for density, which is exactly right for dashboards.
topics.data_idea: Creates seeded metric series with trends and noise, renders a sparkline per metric, and pairs each with its latest value and change.
topics.name: Sparkline Table Builder
topics.real_world_use: Monitoring dashboards show sparkline columns so on-call engineers spot degrading metrics instantly.

topics.concept: A histogram bins continuous values and shows the shape of a distribution: normal, skewed, or bimodal. In ASCII, each bin becomes a bar, and choosing bin width is the key judgment call. It reveals at a glance whether data behaves the way a model assumes.
topics.data_idea: Samples seeded distributions including normal, skewed, and bimodal mixes, bins them with configurable width, and renders the ASCII histogram with summary stats.
topics.name: ASCII Histogram Renderer
topics.real_world_use: Analysts check histograms during data QA to catch skew and outliers before modeling.

topics.concept: Pie charts show parts of a whole, and in a terminal they become labeled bars with percentage shares instead of slices. They work only when categories are few and shares differ clearly; too many thin slices become unreadable. The honest rule is to switch to bars when precision matters.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded share data across a few categories, renders labeled percentage bars, and warns when categories are too many for the format.

key_params.sort: whether to order slices by size

topics.name: Terminal Share Chart
topics.real_world_use: CLI budget tools show spending shares with this format for quick allocation reviews.

topics.concept: A progress panel shows several goals at once as labeled bars with percent-complete and targets. Color-free ASCII markers like brackets and hashes keep it readable in any terminal. It turns a status meeting into a single glanceable screen.
topics.data_idea: Creates seeded goals with targets and current values, renders a multi-row progress panel with completion percentages and behind-pace flags.
topics.name: Goal Progress Panel
topics.real_world_use: Teams display progress panels in standups to track OKRs and sprint goals.

topics.concept: A stem-and-leaf plot is the original text histogram: stems hold the leading digits and leaves the trailing ones, preserving actual values while showing shape. It teaches distribution thinking without any graphics. Analysts still use it for quick exploratory looks at small datasets.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded small numeric datasets, builds the stem-and-leaf layout, and annotates median and quartiles inline.
topics.name: Stem and Leaf Plotter
topics.real_world_use: Statistics instructors use stem-and-leaf plots to teach distributions hands-on.

topics.concept: An ASCII scatter plot places points on a character grid, revealing correlation, clusters, and outliers in two variables. Overplotting is handled by density characters so dense regions read darker. It is the quickest exploratory check before fitting any model.
topics.data_idea: Samples seeded correlated and clustered point clouds, renders them on a character grid with density shading, and reports correlation per cloud.

key_params.grid_size: rows and columns of the grid

topics.name: ASCII Scatter Plotter
topics.real_world_use: Data scientists sketch scatter plots in notebooks and CLI EDA before choosing models.

topics.concept: A gauge shows one number against its target range: a needle or filled arc marking where the value sits between minimum and maximum. In text form it becomes a scaled bar with threshold zones for good, warning, and critical. One well-placed gauge beats a table of numbers for status-at-a-glance.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded KPI values with target bands, renders ASCII gauges with zone coloring via characters, and flags values outside tolerance.
topics.name: Terminal KPI Gauge
topics.real_world_use: Operations dashboards use gauges for headline metrics like uptime and capacity headroom.

topics.concept: A funnel chart stacks conversion stages as narrowing bars, making drop-off between steps instantly visible. The steepest narrowing points to the biggest leak. Labeling each step with both counts and conversion rates keeps the chart honest about where users actually leave.
topics.data_idea: Simulates seeded user flows through named stages with stage-specific drop-off, renders the ASCII funnel, and highlights the steepest conversion drop.
topics.name: Conversion Funnel Visualizer
topics.real_world_use: Growth teams review funnel charts weekly to prioritize onboarding and checkout fixes.

topics.concept: A Pareto chart orders causes by frequency and overlays the cumulative share, making the vital few visible: often 20 percent of causes drive 80 percent of problems. The cumulative line crossing 80 percent marks where to stop investigating and start fixing. It focuses improvement effort where it pays most.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded defect or ticket causes with skewed frequencies, renders ranked bars with the cumulative line, and marks the 80 percent cutoff.
topics.name: Pareto Chart Builder
topics.real_world_use: Quality teams use Pareto charts to pick which defect causes to attack first.

topics.concept: A correlation heatmap colors a matrix of pairwise correlations so strong relationships pop out as color blocks. It is the standard first look at a multivariate dataset before modeling. In a terminal, characters of increasing density stand in for color intensity.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded correlated feature sets, computes the correlation matrix, and renders it as a density-character heatmap with the strongest pairs listed.
topics.name: Correlation Heatmap Simulator
topics.real_world_use: Analysts scan correlation heatmaps to spot multicollinearity before regression.

topics.concept: A Gantt chart lays project tasks as horizontal bars across a timeline, showing overlaps, sequencing, and the critical path. Even a text version communicates schedule risk: stacked bars reveal resource conflicts and long chains. It remains the clearest way to answer when everything finishes.
topics.data_idea: Creates a seeded project with task durations and dependencies, computes start and end dates, renders the ASCII timeline, and highlights the critical path.
topics.name: Terminal Gantt Chart
topics.real_world_use: Project managers share Gantt views in status reports to make schedules tangible.

topics.concept: A dual-axis chart plots two series with different scales, like revenue and margin percent, sharing one timeline. It invites insight but also invites distortion, so honest versions anchor both axes at meaningful baselines and label scales clearly. Used carefully, it shows relationships that separate charts hide.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded paired series with different units, renders both on one ASCII timeline with labeled dual scales, and reports their correlation.

key_params.points: time points shared by both series

topics.name: Dual Axis Chart Builder
topics.real_world_use: Finance presentations pair revenue with margin on dual axes to show profitable growth.

topics.concept: Small multiples repeat the same chart for each segment in a grid, so the eye compares shapes instead of reading numbers. A dozen mini trend lines reveal which regions or products deviate. Consistent scales across panels are mandatory, or the comparison lies.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded time series per segment with a few planted anomalies, renders a grid of mini ASCII line charts on shared scales, and flags deviating panels.
topics.name: Small Multiples Grid
topics.real_world_use: Regional managers compare small-multiple sales trends to spot underperforming territories.

topics.concept: A radar chart plots several dimensions as spokes, with each entity forming a polygon that reveals its profile shape. It suits comparing a handful of entities across the same five to eight criteria. The honest caveat is that spoke order changes the shape, so dimensions should follow a meaningful sequence.
topics.data_idea: Creates seeded entity scores across named dimensions, renders ASCII radar polygons, and computes profile similarity between entities.
topics.name: Radar Profile Chart
topics.real_world_use: Vendor evaluations compare radar profiles across capability dimensions.

topics.concept: A treemap fills a rectangle with nested boxes sized by value, showing hierarchical composition at a glance. In ASCII, boxes become bordered regions with labels sized to fit. It beats a long ranked list when the question is how the whole divides into parts.
topics.data_idea: Generates a seeded category hierarchy with values, lays out nested ASCII boxes by area, and labels each region with its share.
topics.name: ASCII Treemap Renderer
topics.real_world_use: Portfolio reviews use treemaps to show allocation across asset classes.

topics.concept: An animated cohort heatmap plays retention forward month by month, so viewers watch cohorts fade or hold over time. Animation adds the time dimension a static heatmap compresses. It is particularly persuasive for showing that a product change bent the retention curve.
topics.data_idea: Simulates seeded cohort retention with a mid-history improvement event, renders frame-by-frame ASCII heatmaps, and marks the intervention month.
topics.name: Cohort Heatmap Animator
topics.real_world_use: Growth teams animate retention to demonstrate the impact of onboarding redesigns.

topics.concept: A Sankey diagram draws flows between stages with widths proportional to volume, showing where users, money, or materials actually go. In text form, flows become labeled bands whose widths scale with throughput. It exposes the real paths through a system, which are rarely the designed ones.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded flow volumes between process stages, renders ASCII bands scaled by volume, and lists the dominant and leak paths.
topics.name: Flow Sankey Simulator
topics.real_world_use: Energy and web-analytics teams use Sankeys to trace where resources flow and leak.

topics.concept: A control chart plots a process metric over time with upper and lower control limits computed from its own variation. Points outside the limits signal special causes worth investigating; everything inside is normal noise. It stops teams from overreacting to every wiggle while catching real shifts.
topics.data_idea: Simulates a seeded process with in-control noise plus injected shifts, computes control limits, renders the ASCII chart, and flags out-of-control points.
topics.name: SPC Control Chart
topics.real_world_use: Manufacturing quality teams run control charts to distinguish noise from real process changes.

topics.concept: Candlestick charts pack open, high, low, and close into one glyph per period, showing the battle between buyers and sellers. In ASCII, wicks and bodies are drawn with vertical characters and blocks. Reading sequences of candles reveals momentum, reversals, and indecision without any price feed graphics.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded OHLC series with trend and volatility regimes, renders ASCII candlesticks, and labels classic patterns like dojis and engulfing bars.
topics.name: Terminal Candlestick Chart
topics.real_world_use: Traders scan candlestick charts to read intraday momentum and reversal signals.

topics.concept: A network graph lays nodes and edges in text, revealing clusters, hubs, and bridges in relationships. ASCII layout uses simple placement heuristics since true graph layout is heavy. Even a rough rendering exposes the most connected nodes and isolated groups.
topics.data_idea: Generates a seeded graph with planted communities, computes centrality scores, renders an ASCII layout, and lists hub nodes and bridges.
topics.name: ASCII Network Graph
topics.real_world_use: Analysts sketch network views to find key connectors in organizations or systems.

topics.concept: A violin plot shows a full distribution as a mirrored density shape with a box plot inside, revealing skew and multimodality that a box alone hides. In ASCII, density becomes symmetric character widths per row. Comparing violins side by side is the richest quick comparison of several groups.
topics.data_idea: Samples seeded groups with different distribution shapes, estimates densities, renders ASCII violins with quartile markers, and reports shape differences.
topics.name: Violin Plot Simulator
topics.real_world_use: Researchers compare violin plots to see distribution shifts across experimental conditions.

topics.concept: A dashboard composer assembles multiple ASCII charts into one coherent screen: KPIs on top, trends in the middle, breakdowns below. Layout rules keep it readable: one message per panel, shared time ranges, and no more than six panels. It proves that good dashboarding is about editing, not adding.
topics.data_idea: Builds a seeded business dataset, renders a composed multi-panel ASCII dashboard with KPI header, trend charts, and breakdowns, and validates layout rules.
topics.name: Terminal Dashboard Composer
topics.real_world_use: SRE and ops teams build terminal dashboards for environments where browsers are unavailable.

topics.concept: A waterfall chart shows how a starting value becomes an ending value through sequential positive and negative steps. Each bar floats from the running total, making bridges between plan and actual intuitive. It is the standard visual for explaining variance, one driver at a time.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded bridge components from a starting value to an ending value, renders the floating ASCII bars, and labels each step's contribution.
topics.name: Waterfall Bridge Chart
topics.real_world_use: FP&A teams present waterfall bridges to explain how results moved from forecast to actual.
